infoMrtBody: The Airport metro (MRT) connects Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport directly to Taipei. Take the express or commuter train from Terminal 1 or Terminal 2 to Taipei Main Station — the journey takes around 35 minutes. From Taipei Main Station you can connect to the red (Danshui–Xinyi) or green (Songshan–Xindian) lines to reach your hotel.
infoUberBody: Uber is widely available in Taipei and is a convenient option from the airport. Simply open the app and request a ride as you normally would.
infoWeatherBody: Late March in Taipei is mild spring — around 18–24°C. It can be rainy, so pack a light jacket and a small umbrella.
infoCurrencyBody: The local currency is the New Taiwan Dollar (TWD). Cash is still widely used at night markets and smaller restaurants, so it's worth having some on hand. ATMs are easy to find throughout the city.
infoEasyCardBody: An EasyCard (悠遊卡) is a reloadable transit card that works on the MRT and buses — similar to an Oyster card. Pick one up at the airport or any MRT station.
infoPlugsBody: Taiwan uses 110V with US-style flat two-pin plugs (Type A). European guests will need a travel adapter.
infoTapWaterBody: Tap water in Taipei is not recommended for drinking. Bottled water is inexpensive and available everywhere, including all convenience stores.
infoConvenienceBody: 7-Eleven and FamilyMart are on virtually every corner, open 24/7. They sell hot food, snacks, SIM cards, and have ATMs — genuinely useful for day-to-day needs.
infoSimBody: Prepaid SIM cards with data are available at the airport on arrival from major carriers. Good 4G/5G coverage throughout Taipei.
infoMuslimBody: Taipei has a growing selection of halal-certified restaurants, particularly in the Da'an and Zhongzheng districts. The Taipei Grand Mosque (台北清真大寺), located near Da'an Forest Park, is the city's main mosque and welcomes visitors. Several restaurants near the mosque serve halal food. Many international chains also offer halal options — look for the halal certificate displayed at the entrance.
